html:
The Cuitlatec were a people of the middle Balsas River basin and the Sierra Madre del Sur in today's Guerrero, Mexico. Their language was an isolate, related to no other known language.

In 1492 their country lay on the contested border between the Purépecha kingdom and the Aztec Triple Alliance. After the conquest their numbers fell, and Spanish and Nahuatl took over. The language was last spoken in the town of San Miguel Totolapan and is now extinct. Their neighbours included the Chontal of Guerrero.
